premises: Refractory carbide particles (e.g., HfC, ZrC) can be formed and uniformly dispersed at the nanoscale in a refractory HEA via composition and processing adjustments.
Nanoscale carbide precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding.
The carbide dispersion will increase yield strength and creep resistance at high temperatures (>1000°C).
The carbide dispersion will not degrade the alloy's inherent thermal and irradiation stability (phase stability under high irradiation flux).
The improvement holds provided particles remain uniformly fine (<~100 nm) and do not coarsen or aggregate.
